title: 1954 AHSME Problem 49
statement: The difference of the squares of two odd numbers is always divisible by \(8.\) If \(a>b,\) and \(2a+1\) and \(2b+1\) are the odd numbers, to prove the given statement we put the difference of the squares in the form:

solutions.text:
Expanding and regrouping, \[ \begin{aligned} &(2a+1)^2-(2b+1)^2\\ &\qquad=4[a(a+1)-b(b+1)]. \end{aligned} \] Each of \(a(a+1)\) and \(b(b+1)\) is even, so their difference is even. The displayed expression is consequently divisible by \(4\cdot2=8.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Expand the two squares and group each variable with its successor
